newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Foreigners net buyers in Colombo stocks - Exchange.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners net buyers in Colombo stocks - Exchange.

text.p: The level of foreign participation in Colombo's stock market rose sharply in April, a report by the Colombo Stock Exchange showed.
"Foreign investor participation accounted for 45 percent of the total turnover with a net inflow of 258 million rupees," the exchange said in a report seen by Reuters on Tuesday.
Net foreign inflows in March totalled 25.6 million rupees, accounting for 38 percent of the turnover.

"The indices reached their highest level since August 1995 in April, with the all share index appreciating 102 points (16 percent), while the sensitive index gained 195 points (20 percent)," the report said.

Analysts link the recent rise to good company growth expectations, a three percent cut in reserve ratios at commercial banks and an agreement between the government and the opposition to work together to end the nation's ethnic conflict.
"Daily average turnover stood at 118 million rupees in April compared to the previous month's figure of 49.8 million," the report said.
It said plantation sector stocks recorded the sharpest rise, adding 29 percent in the month.
"The banking sector rose 19 percent while diversified holdings rose 14 percent, hotels 19 percent and the manufacturing sector 13 percent," the report said.
